candidates.title: Any paid plan price satisfies the payment amount check — pay cheapest tier price, receive most expensive plan for 30 days
candidates.description: CreatePaymentQuery validates an MP payment's transaction_amount against `accepted_amounts`, which is the UNION of every non-trial plan price plus pending_charge — not the amount corresponding to the plan/charge actually being granted. A payment whose amount equals ANY plan's price is accepted and ApplyPendingPlanQuery then applies whatever pending_plan_suscription (or the pending_payment plan_suscription) is set, granting the most expensive plan while collecting the cheapest plan's price. The broad acceptance was added deliberately to avoid orphaned MP charges when a debit/preference was issued before a plan change ('un debito MP realineado tarde sale al monto viejo'), but it decouples amount from entitlement in both directions. Exploit is deterministic: (a) pending_payment subscription — create checkout preference at cheap plan, PATCH plan to expensive (pending_payment branch rewrites plan_suscription directly), pay the stale cheap preference -> expensive plan ACTIVE 30d; (b) active subscription — create checkout preference at current cheap plan price, then request upgrade to expensive plan (pending_plan + prorated pending_charge), pay the stale cheap preference -> paid_amount != pending_charge so it is treated as full-price -> pending expensive plan applied AND end_date renewed +30d. Repeatable monthly: downgrade-pending legit cheap payment + stale cheap preference + upgrade-pending yields top-tier plan at entry-tier price every cycle. With auto_renew, a failed UpdatePreapprovalPlanQuery realignment leaves MP debiting the old cheap amount and each monthly debit re-triggers the same mismatch.
candidates.root_cause: AdminApp/domains/payments/services/services.py CreatePaymentQuery lines 103-127: `accepted_amounts` unions {pending_plan-or-current price, current plan price, ALL SuscriptionPlan prices where is_trial=False, pending_charge} and only checks membership — the granted entitlement (pending_plan or pending_payment plan) is never bound to the amount paid. `expected_amount` is computed but used only in the error message.
candidates.intended_behavior: A payment should only credit the entitlement its amount pays for: pending_charge for prorated upgrades, or the price of the specific plan being applied (pending_plan if set else plan_suscription for pending_payment). Stale-amount MP charges should either map amount->plan (grant the plan that amount corresponds to) or be rejected/flagged for reconciliation rather than silently upgrading entitlement.

payloads: 4) Pay P1 in MP checkout ($cheap) -> webhook/sync registers Payment amount=cheap APPROVED

candidates.remediation: Bind the accepted amount to the granted entitlement instead of unioning all plan prices. Options: (a) compute expected = pending_charge if set else (pending_plan or plan_suscription).price for pending_payment, accept only that plus the current plan price ONLY when no pending_plan exists (pure renewal), and for genuinely stale debits apply the plan matching the paid amount rather than the pending one; (b) on amount!=expected but amount==some plan price, resolve which plan that price belongs to and grant THAT plan (amount->plan mapping) instead of pending_plan; (c) reject mismatched amount/plan combos and rely on audit_orphan_payments + manual reconciliation for stale MP charges. Also align UpdatePreapprovalPlanQuery failure handling so a stale-amount debit cannot recur monthly.

severity.rationale: Requires deliberate multi-step API use plus a real (lower-tier) payment, but is fully deterministic, needs no provider misbehavior, recurs monthly via the downgrade/upgrade-preference cycle, scales across freely-registrable accounts, and produces fiscally inconsistent invoices (expensive plan name, cheap total). Direct recurring revenue loss bounded by the plan price spread per period.
